quiz.question: What does a loop let you do?

answers.answer: Store a single value that never changes
Write an instruction once and repeat it many times
Give a name to a block of code you can call later
Compare two values to see which is bigger

quiz.explanation: A loop lets you write one instruction and tell the computer to repeat it. This saves you from typing the same line over and over again.

quiz.question: Why would a loop be a better choice than writing the same line 1,000 times?

answers.answer: The loop lets the computer skip some lines to save time
It prevents typos and never gets bored or skips any repetition
Loops are the only way to use numbers in a program
Loops automatically make your code prettier on screen

quiz.explanation: Computers running loops never get tired, never skip, and never make typos even on the 847th repetition. That reliability is why loops beat copy-pasting instructions.
